essence: The longest song is a catalogue proving nothing is outside the festival: tears tasting nectar (1); all acts succeeding, devotees as successes (2); all beings worshipping unceasing (3); touch perfected by meditation (4); equinox-moment always (5); beginningless deed, single resort (6); gods fortunate even in delusion (7); whenever-wherever worship (8); incomparable enjoyers (9); the festival known only by getting (10); worship with all 36 tattva-acts (11); time spent in joy (12); greed growing daily (13); dwelling in His ocean (14); mind offered as sweet (15); senses sent as errands (16); drowning as sole liberation-route (17); perpetual foot-festival as grace-cause (18); moment-by-moment tasting (19); seen fruit (20); untasted happiness till then (21); effortless abiding (22); omnicompetent madness (23); unbegging worship praised (24); everything-is (25); utensil-body (26); dependent self-will (27); thirst quenched into lake (28); devotee as vessel like Him (29); festival agitating the 36 (30); instruments worshipped (31); mantra-placement then rest (32); kingdoms blooming (33); gods-freed-or-someone unanswered (34); lightness and weight (35); milk-ocean churning (36); wish-cow vs inward milking (37); glances feeding (38); lowliness crowned (39); steps for some, spread for devotees (40); divine foothold through madness (41); stunned mind, He alone as vessel (42); full-steady-devoted means (43); organ-host fortune (44); prettiness found (45); rising from formed or formless (46); passions conscripted (47); straw-yet-jewel close (48).

sections.FUNCTION: Proof-by-exhaustion: 48 verses leave nothing outside the festival — acts, actors, instruments, senses, gods, tattvas, passions, straw — so worship needs no defense; it is what everything already is.
sections.KEY TERMS:
* **mahotsava** — great festival: it's single answer to every verse's implicit question.
* **carvaṇa** — chewing/rumination (anticipated; Stotra 20's title): understanding as tasting, tasting as worship.
* **yācñā-absent** — no begging here (contrast Stotra 11): the one song that never asks, only shows.
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Seventeenth song, longest in the set: the festival at full stretch before manifestation (18), dawning (19), and chewing (20) close the collection. Read straight through; do not mine it for theses.
sections.EXPLANATION: The catalogue's order is ritual order: invocation (1–2), congregation (3), rule (4), time (5), ground (6), auspiciousness even in delusion (7), universality (8), incomparability (9), epistemology of participation (10), full apparatus of 36 (11), time spent (12), growing greed (13), dwelling (14), offering mind (15), dispatching senses (16), sole route (17), grace-economics reversed (18), moment-tasting (19), seen fruit (20), retrospective devaluation (21), effortlessness (22), omnicompetence (23), unbegging praise (24), everything-is (25), utensil-body (26), dependent self-will (27), thirst quenched into lake (28), vessel-mirroring (29), cosmic agitation (30), instrument-worship (31), placement-then-rest (32), redistribution (33), status unanswered (34), lightness and weight (35), milk-ocean churning (36), two milking-economies (37), glances feeding (38), lowliness crowned (39), steps vs spread (40), divine foothold through madness (41), stunned mind, He alone as vessel (42), fourfold means (43), organ-fortune (44), prettiness found (45), rising regardless (46), passions conscripted (47), straw-jewel close (48).
sections.BOUNDARY: Verse 34's status question is unanswered by design; verse 41's divine dependence is confessed, not explained. Meter likely mixed across 48 verses — scan before freezing. It proves by showing, not by arguing; do not extract theses from it.
sections.RELATED:
* Stotra 20 (carvaṇa): chewing as a whole song; read the pair.
* Stotra 4, v.2 (lowest ground kept): the festival's seating logic.
* Stotra 12, v.10 (pretense suffices): the minimum entry beside this maximum catalogue.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of festival (utsava); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) at the catalogue of all beings worshipping. The rasa is the bliss of the festival — everything inside, nothing outside. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as ānanda: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute's festival.
